newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Oct 29.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Cricket Board has displayed more green than gold after threatening to ban the major city of New Delhi from any future tours of India until the national capital cleans up its act and reduces air pollution. Team management believes the pollution in the city is so bad it has caused eye and respiratory problems for the cricketers. Page 20.

Following grave fears of sustaining spinal injuries from a training mishap, Wallaby second-rower John Welborn has received a clean bill of health from doctors. It will not be known until the end of the week if the rugby union star can play on Saturday in the team's current Scottish leg of the European tour. Page 20.

Major injury fears continue to plague the Wallaby's European tour team as injured lock Garrick Morgan's return to the game has been set back after developing a blood clot on his lung as a result of a complication after surgery on his fractured ankle. Morgan had been sent home last week after sustaining the fracture in the team's tour of Italy. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

For her Atlanta Olympics three-medal haul, champion swimmer Suzie O'Neill collected A$51,000 from communications giant Telstra as part of the company's athlete incentive scheme. O'Neill also received an additional A$47,000 reward from the Australian Sports Commission for her efforts, confirming O'Neill made the right choice when she decided against retirement before the Atlanta games. Page 44.

More legal turmoil hit rugby when several top NSW Rugby Union Super 12 players refused to accept their contracts. President of the Rugby Union Player's Association Inc, Anthony Dempsey, has described the discretion of the NSWRU to change payments to players under contract as "draconian." Page 44.

The future of the Sydney Marathon is still under a cloud following the decision of creditors of Athletics NSW to allow the financially-troubled body to continue trading. Creditors voted to accept a deed of arrangement following the appointment of an administrator to Athletics NSW after it was revealed an operating deficit of A$121,000 existed. Page 43.
THE AGE

After being invited by the Australian Golf Union, U.S. President Bill Clinton is reputedly keen to play in the Australian Open pro-am tour in Sydney next month - to partner either world number one Greg Norman or US golfing sensation Tiger Woods. Page A1.

The racing world is awaiting champion trainer Bart Cummings' decision on whether Saintly will start in next Tuesday's Melbourne Cup, rather than opting to run in the Japan Cup in Tokyo on 24 November. Cummings is reputedly in two minds about which event to enter rising favourite Saintly. Page C8.

The Victorian Racing Club has taken positive steps to ensure all horses involved in the Melbourne Cup carnival are safe from outside interference before racing. After the discovery of prohibited substance frusemide on Future Shock in last month's Caulfield Cup, extra staff will be patrolling the birdcage area at Flemington to watch over the horses on race days. Page C8.
HERALD SUN

At a cool A$4 million, strong Melbourne Cup favourite Oscar Schindler is on the market. Irish owner Ollie Lehane yesterday confirmed the 7-2 Cup chance was for sale. A syndicate of Victorian breeders offered the golfing-mad owner a reported A$2.5 million for the horse last week. Page 72.

After a failed bid to move to new Australian Football League club Port Adelaide, ex-Hawthorn ruckman Nick Holland has returned to his former team despite previously stating he had resigned and wanted to be traded to another club. Holland happily attended the Hawks' first summer training session last night. Page 70.

Australia's cricketers have called for greater input into programming over future overseas tours following disenchantment with this year's scheduling of tours in India and Sri Lanka. The players want to avoid the Test match against India which occurred after only three days of first-class cricket following an eight month break and they are concerned with the excessive one-day matches in India's triangular Titan Cup series. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The top cricket umpires have requested the Australian Cricket Board studies the bowling style of NSW all-rounder Brad McNamara and Queensland off-spinner Geoff Foley, following doubts over the legality of bowling styles. The umpires allege that both playes "threw" the ball, rather than bowled, during an recent interstate clash. Page 68.

The Australian Rugby League and Super League competitions are set for the first clash of codes on Anzac Day next year. The April 25 date will see the Sydney Football Stadium booked by Super League for an Australia-New Zealand Test while the ARL has confirmed its annual City-Country Origin game for Newcastle's Marathon Stadium on the same day. Page 66.

Champion Australian trainer currently based in Hong Kong, David Hayes, has been required to provide evidence into the territory's largest race-fixing inquires. The inquiry centres on Gold Capture, which some commentators claim was ridden gently. The Hong Kong Jockey Club is notorious for suspending jockeys who do not ensure top placings for their horses. Page 66.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
